key_insight: Marginal Advantage Accumulation (MAA) turns inconsistent batch-level memory feedback into a cross-batch, operation-level evidence signal so stable helpful operations can be separated from accidental ones.
engineering_relevance: For memory-driven agents, MAA offers a practical post-processing layer that improves trace distillation quality while cutting optimization-token cost by about 75%.
method: Build differential signals so operation effects are comparable across batches
Accumulate signed evidence per operation with exponential moving average (EMA)
Merge semantically identical traces to preserve cross-batch identity and traceability
evidence_signal: Across 4 benchmarks and 4 target models, MAA achieved the best results in 14 of 16 settings, outperforming batch-level baselines and often matching or surpassing online methods.
watch_item: Performance depends on reliable semantic identity merging and on whether differential signals remain well-aligned across diverse batch distributions.
paper_title: Marginal Advantage Accumulation for Memory-Driven Agent Self-Evolution
